newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB sees slowing of monetary aggregates in 1997.
newsitem.headline: SNB sees slowing of monetary aggregates in 1997.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) board member Bruno Gehrig said the central bank expected a slowdown this year in the growth of all the monetary aggregates that it follows as a guide for setting monetary policy.
Gehrig said monetary aggregates had first reacted to the SNB's more expansive monetary policy by expanding. This expansion occurred after the SNB adopted an easier monetary policy stance in 1995.
Falling interest rates had caused the monetary aggregates to expand, he noted.
"Our expectation is that the interest-rate related increase is now slowing," Gehrig told reporters after a speech here.
This slowdown would be first be noticed in the wider aggregates and signs of this was already in evidence, he added.
